task.title: Never move the newest-release surfaces backward when publishing
task.description:
Split out of "Cut patch releases to an older line without releasing main" (2026-10-10), which depends on it.

Publishing a release today assumes it is the newest one. GitHub marks every newly published release Latest, publish-release.sh refreshes the Homebrew tap formula unconditionally, release.yml cascades every v* tag into a desktop tag, and publish-desktop-release.sh moves the rolling desktop-latest release (the site download links and the auto-updater address) to whatever desktop tag it publishes. That is already a bug: a dispatched rerun of an older desktop tag moves desktop-latest backward. It becomes a certain one once older-line patch releases exist.

Add one version comparison (for example scripts/release-is-newest.sh, comparing against the newest stable v* / desktop-v* tag; pre-releases follow their own existing rules) and gate on it:
- publish-release.sh: `gh release edit --latest` only when newest, otherwise `--latest=false`; skip the tap commit when the release is not newest, and also when the tap formula already carries a higher version.
- release.yml desktop-tag job: skip the desktop cascade with a notice, rather than failing in plan-desktop-release.sh, when the release is not the newest.
- publish-desktop-release.sh: publish the versioned desktop release but move desktop-latest only when the tag is the newest desktop-v* tag.
- release.yml: validate the tag sits on a supported branch: reachable from origin/main with no higher stable tag as its ancestor. (The maint/vX.Y line-branch case is added by the dependent story.)

Decided with Dylan: an older patch is a quiet release: visible on the Releases page, but Latest, the site's desktop download, the desktop auto-updater and brew install all stay on the newest release, and no desktop build is published for an older line.

Tests in scripts/*_test.go with local bare remotes and the gh stub: an older release passes --latest=false and makes no tap commit; a newer formula in the tap is skipped; an older desktop tag publishes its versioned release without force-moving or uploading to desktop-latest; the newest release behaves exactly as today. Update release_workflow_test.go's guard list and assert the desktop-tag job is gated.
